source: Kosinski (2023/2024, PNAS) Evaluating large language models in theory of mind tasks
finding: Eleven LLMs were given 40 false-belief tasks. Each task had a false-belief scenario, 3 true-belief controls and reversed versions; all 8 had to be solved. Newer GPT models solve more.
numbers: Older models solved 0 tasks. GPT-3 davinci-003 and ChatGPT-3.5-turbo solved 20%. ChatGPT-4 solved 75%, said to match 6-year-old children.
quote: ToM-like ability ... may have emerged as an unintended by-product of LLMs' improving language skills
limits: Text-only unexpected-contents and unexpected-transfer tasks; shortcuts possible; later work breaks it (c02, c03).
agent_relevance: Base rate for LLM false-belief tracking. The animal root of this test is what others see and know.

source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks
finding: Small changes that keep the ToM logic intact flip GPT-3.5 answers. Examples: a transparent container so the protagonist can see inside, or an uninformative label.
numbers: Transparent-bag variant: model still says she believes chocolate (about 95-98%) although she can see popcorn. Transparent-chest cat task: still says John looks in the old place (90-94%).
limits: Hand-made variations, one model family. Argues the null hypothesis should be skeptical.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of the animal control that changes what the other can see. Models follow the story script, not line of sight.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? Stress Testing Social Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Six ToM tasks plus adversarial variants of Kosinski's set. LLMs show some ToM but not robustly. They fail on adversarial examples and on datasets built to block artifacts.
numbers: GPT-4 reaches 97% on the original false-belief items but falls to 0% on 'transparent access' and 'inon' variants (davinci-002 had 66.7% on transparent access). Probing method matters: 7 point gap for GPT-4 between multiple-choice and CoT on SocialIQa.
quote: caution against drawing conclusions from anecdotal examples
limits: Probing format (MC vs generative vs CoT) shifts results.
agent_relevance: Clever Hans framing from animal work. Add transparent-access and relationship-change controls when testing an agent's model of another mind.

source: Sap, Le Bras, Fried, Choi (2022) Neural Theory-of-Mind? On the Limits of Social Intelligence in Large LMs
finding: GPT-3 lacks social intelligence out of the box on SocialIQa and ToMi.
numbers: 55% on SocialIQa and 60% on ToMi, well below human.
limits: Pre-ChatGPT model; newer models score higher.
agent_relevance: The answer depends on model generation; re-test each new model.

source: Gandhi, Franken, Gerstenberg, Goodman (2023) Understanding Social Reasoning in LMs with LMs (BigToM)
finding: BigToM has 25 controls and 5,000 model-written items from causal templates (forward belief, forward action, backward belief). GPT-4 mirrors human inference patterns, less reliably; other LLMs struggle.
numbers: GPT-4 0-shot: forward belief about .97-.99; backward belief false-belief .53 (true-belief .86); humans 82% true-belief and 72% false-belief backward. One-shot CoT lifts GPT-4 backward false-belief to .75-.85. Zero-shot CoT inconsistent.
quote: mimicking the reasoning template is enough to solve our task in most cases
limits: Authors warn demo-CoT gains may not mean stronger ToM. Humans got instructions and one demo.
agent_relevance: Few-shot templates help but may be imitation. Backward inference (what did they see?) is hardest, like inferring what a rival jay saw.

source: Kim et al. (2023) FANToM: A Benchmark for Stress-testing Machine Theory of Mind in Interactions
finding: Conversations with information asymmetry (a person leaves, then returns). The same reasoning is asked in several question types. Models do belief multiple-choice better than the linked list questions, so ToM looks illusory.
numbers: Human scores: ALL 87.5, answerability list 90.6, info-access list 90.6. GPT-4 0613 + CoT ALL 26.6 (Jun) or 14.8 (Oct); ChatGPT 0613 + CoT 3.7; Llama-2 chat + CoT 0.4. Models trail humans by over 70 points on average.
limits: Fine-tuning gives scores near human on one format but does not generalise.
agent_relevance: Audit consistency across who-knows-what questions before trusting an agent's belief about others.

source: Wilf et al. (2023) Think Twice: Perspective-Taking Improves LLM Theory-of-Mind (SimToM)
finding: Two-stage prompt: first filter the story to what the character knows, then answer. Based on simulation theory. Beats zero-shot and CoT.
numbers: BigToM false belief, GPT-3.5: 41.0 (0-shot), 56.25 (CoT), 70.5 SimToM (+29.5, +14.2). ToMi false belief GPT-4: 25.5, 74.25, 87.75 (+62.2, +13.5). Llama2-13b up to +47 over CoT on ToMi FB. Oracle perspective-taking: ToMi FB 81.0 to 96.0; BigToM FB 70.5 to 96.0.
limits: Two prompts per item; templated benchmarks; some 0-shot drops come from answer parsing.
agent_relevance: Cheapest scaffold found: restrict context to what the other party could perceive, then reason. A 'perspective filter' operator, the code form of what the rival jay saw.

source: Sclar et al. (2023) Minding Language Models' (Lack of) Theory of Mind: SymbolicToM
finding: Decoding-time plug-in that keeps an explicit graph of who believes what (including beliefs about beliefs) and feeds the relevant slice to the model. No training.
numbers: ToMi: +62 accuracy points on first-order false-belief for Flan-T5-XL; +78 points on second-order false-belief for GPT-3.5. Near-perfect kept on non-ToM questions.
limits: Narrow template benchmark; authors found spurious patterns in ToMi.
agent_relevance: An explicit per-observer belief store is a tool the agent loop can use.

source: Street et al. (2024) LLMs achieve adult human performance on higher-order theory of mind tasks
finding: Handwritten Multi-Order ToM Q&A, 7 stories; five LLMs against a new adult human sample. GPT-4 and Flan-PaLM near adult level; GPT-4 beats humans at 6th order.
numbers: ToM-statement accuracy: humans 90.4% (fact 97.5%), Flan-PaLM 84.3%, GPT-4 88.6%, GPT-3.5 52.5%, PaLM 59.3%, LaMDA 50%. 6th order: GPT-4 93% vs humans 82%.
limits: Written true/false statements; robustness studies dispute the broad claim.
agent_relevance: Recursion depth is not the bottleneck; applying knowledge is (c10).

source: Gu et al. (2024; ICLR 2026) SimpleToM: Exposing the Gap Between Explicit ToM Inference and Implicit ToM Application
finding: Everyday stories with hidden information. Models infer awareness correctly but fail to use it for behaviour prediction or judgment.
numbers: Mental-state question over 95% for GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-405B, Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Behaviour prediction at least 30 points lower; GPT-3.5 7.6%. Judgment 10-24.9% (below chance) for those models; best DeepSeek-R1 65.8%. o1-preview 84.1% on prediction. A mental-state reminder lifts prediction above 80% but judgment stays 42.2% (GPT-4o), 25.8% (Llama-405B).
limits: Binary questions, chance 50%. No simple test-time fix.
agent_relevance: Knowing what the other knows is not acting on it. Add an explicit 'apply it' step and test it.

source: Chen et al. (2024) ToMBench: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in LLMs
finding: Bilingual, built-from-scratch benchmark: 8 tasks, 31 abilities, multiple-choice, no leakage. Best LLMs trail humans by over 10 points.
numbers: Human 85.4% vs GPT-4-1106 75.3% (gap 10.1) and GPT-4-0613 about 10.8 below. CoT adds about nothing (GPT-4-0613 72.8 with CoT vs 73.5 without, approximate table read).
limits: Multiple choice; ability labels set by authors.
agent_relevance: Plain CoT does not fix ToM on a broad benchmark.

source: Hagendorff (2023/2024) Deception Abilities Emerged in Large Language Models
finding: Tests whether models understand and produce false beliefs in others (tactical deception, close to corvid re-caching against a watcher). GPT-4 is strong at first order; second-order deception is weak; CoT amplifies it.
numbers: GPT-4 first-order false recommendation 99.17%, false label 97.50%; second-order false belief 98.75%. Second-order deception: GPT-4 only 11.67% (false recommendation) and 62.08% (false label). Older models FLAN-T5 46.46%, BLOOM 54.79%, curie 65.42%.
limits: Text scenarios, temperature near 0; CoT effect read from a figure.
agent_relevance: Understanding an observer is ahead of using it strategically. Safety relevant.

source: Hu, Sosa, Ullman (2025) Re-evaluating Theory of Mind evaluation in LLMs
finding: Disagreement over LLM ToM comes from not saying whether models should match human behaviour or the human computation. Cites the animal debate (Hare 2001, Kaminski 2008, Heyes 1998).
numbers: No new accuracy numbers.
quote: whether models should be expected to match human behaviors, or the computations underlying those behaviors
limits: Position paper.
agent_relevance: Same behaviour-versus-mentalising split that divides corvid researchers. Define success before testing the agent.

source: Rane et al. (2025, ICML position) Principles of Animal Cognition for LLM Evaluations: A Case Study on Transitive Inference
finding: Five principles from animal cognition (Clever Hans, Morgan's canon, control tasks, failure patterns) applied to GPT-4o on transitive inference. Strip cues one by one and the score drops.
numbers: GPT-4o: A vs C 1.00; ranked animal 0.97; random string 0.92 (SD .09); reverse ranked animal 0.78 (SD .20); trial-based n-term 0.40 (about chance).
limits: Single model, single task; anonymous draft.
agent_relevance: A recipe: remove one cue at a time, as animal studies do. Use it for every social-cognition probe.

source: Bhandari et al. (2026) Caching for the Future: Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles for Agent Memory Systems (ScrubJay-MEM)
finding: Agent memory store inspired by scrub-jay What-Where-When caching: per-memory perishability, a Prospective Memory Buffer, retroactive revision. Used inside an LLM agent loop.
numbers: Temporal Generalization Test (20 instances, 1,320 queries): GenGap +0.108 vs about -0.022 for flat retrieval; decay ablation collapses GenGap 5.7x. EventQA-64k F1 61.58, +2.66 over Mem0, +3.09 over Qwen3-Embedding-4B.
limits: Memory, not social cognition. Gains narrow with stronger backbones and reverse on fact-consolidation tasks.
agent_relevance: The one corvid-to-agent import found. Type-based decay of stale facts is usable.

source: Cross et al. (2024; ICLR 2025) Hypothetical Minds: Scaffolding Theory of Mind for Multi-Agent Tasks with LLMs
finding: LLM agent with a ToM module that writes hypotheses about other agents' strategies, scores them by how well they predict behaviour, and refines them. Tested in Melting Pot.
numbers: Beats LLM-agent and RL baselines over 30 scenarios (competitive, mixed-motive, collaborative); GPT-4 base best. Ablation: removing hypothesis evaluation and refinement hurts.
limits: Game environments, not human mental states; exact reward values not extracted.
agent_relevance: A working loop: predict the other agent, score the guess, refine. Fits an observer-model operator.

source: Amodio, Farrar, Krupenye, Ostojic, Clayton (2021, eLife) Little evidence that Eurasian jays protect their caches by responding to cues about a conspecific's desire and visual perspective
finding: Five experiments with 14 jays failed to replicate Legg and Clayton (2014) and Ostojic et al. (2017). No effect of observer desire or line of sight on caching.
numbers: Exp 1 (9 to 7 birds) W=13 p=0.21; Exp 2 (8 to 7) p=0.83; Exp 3 observed vs private median 0.71 vs 0.54 p=0.59; Exp 4 direct replication Z=0.15 p=0.56; Exp 5 p=0.18.
quote: do not seem to be reliable enough to form the basis for follow-up studies
limits: Small samples, low power; motivation may have changed over about 5 years; authors say it does not refute the ability.
agent_relevance: The corvid results used as the template for machine tests are shaky. Do not treat jay mindreading as settled.

source: Ma et al. (2023/2024) Towards a Holistic Landscape of Situated Theory of Mind in LLMs
finding: Position paper: 7 mental-state categories for machine ToM, benchmark gaps, and a call for situated evaluation where the LLM acts as an agent. Only the abstract was seen.
numbers: 7 mental-state categories; no numbers read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Pointer for a checklist of mental-state types beyond beliefs.

source: Kaminski, Call, Tomasello (2008) Chimpanzees know what others know, but not what they believe (cited in Hu et al. 2025)
finding: Cited as the basis for the split: apes track what others know, not false beliefs. Not opened; only the citation seen.
numbers: none read
limits: Citation only.
agent_relevance: Knowledge tracking is the floor for a social agent; false belief is the extra step LLM tests probe.

source: Hare, Call, Tomasello (2001) Do chimpanzees know what conspecifics know? (cited in Hu et al. 2025)
finding: Cited as the competitor-can-or-cannot-see-food paradigm. Not opened here.
numbers: none read
limits: Citation only.
agent_relevance: Template for a competitor-sees-the-resource probe for agents.

source: Cross-paper synthesis: effect of prompts on ToM
finding: Plain zero-shot CoT is inconsistent for ToM (BigToM, FANToM, ToMBench, SimpleToM). Perspective filtering and symbolic belief tracking give large gains. A mental-state reminder helps prediction, not judgment.
numbers: SimToM +14.2 over CoT (GPT-3.5, BigToM FB); SymbolicToM +62 and +78 points on ToMi; ToMBench CoT about 0 gain; SimpleToM reminder: judgment stays 25.8-42.2%.
limits: Different datasets, models and years; compared by this note.
agent_relevance: Prefer structured scaffolds (filter by perception, explicit belief store) to 'think step by step'.

source: Cross-paper synthesis: stating versus applying
finding: Animal studies test behaviour use (does the subject act on what the rival saw), not reports. LLMs show a matching gap. Street finds GPT-4 at 93% on 6th-order ToM; Hagendorff finds 11.67% on second-order false recommendation deception.
numbers: SimpleToM: awareness over 95% vs judgment 10-24.9%. Street 93% vs Hagendorff 11.67%.
limits: Analogy by this note; not a measured comparison with corvids.
agent_relevance: Probe with action-based tasks, not only question answering.

source: Kosinski (2023/2024) control design and its weakness
finding: Kosinski reads next-word probabilities. Controls: reversed story, correct label, informed protagonist, prefix only. GPT-4 gives P(popcorn)=100% for the content prompt.
numbers: Readouts in text: content prompt P(popcorn)=100%; reversed version about 99.7%; prefix-only control: popcorn 0%, money 79.5%, gems 23.7% in separate completions.
limits: Ullman (c02) shows the same readout breaks under transparent variants.
agent_relevance: Use probability readouts plus matched controls; a single correct answer is weak evidence.

source: Ullman (2023) lesson on null hypothesis
finding: Argues the zero hypothesis for intuitive-psychology tests of models should be skeptical and that outlying failures should outweigh average success. Compares to a calculator-like failure on multiplication.
numbers: Variants tested include transparent access (1A/2A) and uninformative label (1B); models keep predicting the story script.
quote: outlying failure cases should outweigh average success rates
limits: One paper, GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Report the worst variant, not the mean.

source: Bhandari et al. (2026) ScrubJay-MEM design components
finding: Cites Clayton and Dickinson (1998) on jays recovering worms when fresh and peanuts when worms have rotted, and Raby et al. (2007) future-oriented caching, as the source of its memory features.
numbers: Decay ablation collapses GenGap by 5.7x (abstract); full-system GenGap +0.108.
limits: Ablation magnitude taken from the abstract only.
agent_relevance: Backward link: the animal studies behind the method are Clayton and Dickinson (1998) and Raby (2007).
